newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Sentiment mixed on more losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Sentiment mixed on more losses.

text.p: Options analysts remained mixed Monday on whether the U.S. stock market faced more near-term downside or a recovery.
They agreed that Monday was largely a wash as investors and traders awaited the March U.S. consumer price report, due Tuesday before the market opens.
"Today is just a bridge from Friday to tomorrow," said Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services.
Last Friday's report of March producer prices brought a quick end to the market's attempted rebound.
The Dow industrial average ended Friday down 148 points at about 6,392. At early Monday afternoon the blue chip measure was off another 27 points at 6,364.
At the same time the broader S&P 500 index was down about three points at 735 and June S&P 500 futures were up half a point at 739 after falling to 737.60.
One firm pegged June S&P 500 fair value at 5.35 points premium to cash, buy programs at 6.40 points premium and sell programs at 2.50 points premium.
Hegarty said he expected the market to slide further Tuesday after the economic data.

Economists on average expect consumer prices to be up 0.2 percent in March and up 0.3 percent excluding food and energy prices. Prices rose 0.3 percent in February overall and 0.2 percent excluding food and energy.
Analysts said a combination of the economic numbers, the rising onslaught of first quarter company earnings and this week's expiration of April options would likely keep volatility high.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, priced off S&P 100 index options, was up 0.36 at 22.57 Monday after having risen to 23.29 earlier.

Hegarty said the market's "two steps down, one step up" action since the peak in March has allowed retail investors to remain complacent "and believe in their buy-the-dip approach, which inevitably is going to cause them disaster."
Concern appeared to be creeping up Monday, where OEX put volume topped call volume by 103,838 to 91,602 at midday.
Analysts at the Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati said in a report Monday that fear is on the rise.

"The pricing of out-of-the-money OEX puts versus calls has swung heavily to the put side from where it was last month, indicating that there is a strong preference to buy OEX puts rather than calls," the firm said.

Some sentiment indicators are beginning to show higher levels of bearishness, it said. "The combination of technical support, oversold indexes and a large rise in negativity bodes well for the market in the near term."
Lawrence McMillan of McMillan Analysis Corp said the market is oversold but "should be respected as a bear until some real signs of stability have been encountered."
